'''James Ellsworth Ferrell''' (born November 3, 1955) is an American [[Systems biology|systems biologist]].  He is a Professor of Chemical and Systems Biology and Biochemistry at [[Stanford University School of Medicine]].  He was Chair of the Dept. of Chemical and Systems Biology from its inception in 2006 until 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Department renamed to reflect shift in focus|url=https://news.stanford.edu/news/2006/october18/med-name-101806.html|publisher=Stanford University|date=2006-10-18|access-date=2015-03-06}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Ferrell was raised in the Chicago and Pittsburgh areas before graduating from [[Mt. Lebanon High School]] in 1972. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Ferrell Lab Site » People |url=https://ferrelllab.stanford.edu/people/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=ferrelllab.stanford.edu}}</ref>

==Education==

Ferrell was an undergraduate at [[Williams College]], majoring in Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics, and graduated in 1976.  He received his Ph.D. degree in chemistry from [[Stanford University]] in 1984 for work in the laboratory of Wray H. Huestis on the control of red cell shape, and received his M.D. degree from [[Stanford]] in 1986.  He carried out postdoctoral work on signal transduction in the laboratory of G. Steven Martin at [[UC Berkeley]].{{citation needed|date=July 2018}}

==Research==
{{BLP primary sources|section|date=July 2018}}
Through studies of Xenopus laevis oocyte maturation, Ferrell showed how graded changes in the inductive stimulus progesterone are converted into irreversible, all-or-none changes in MAP kinase activity, cyclin-dependent kinase activity, and cell fate.<ref>{{cite journal |pmid=8816754 |pmc=38339 |year=1996 |last1=Huang |first1=C. Y |title=Ultrasensitivity in the mitogen-activated protein kinase cascade |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America |volume=93 |issue=19 |pages=10078–83 |last2=Ferrell Jr |first2=J. E |doi=10.1073/pnas.93.19.10078|bibcode=1996PNAS...9310078H |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/science.280.5365.895 |pmid=9572732 |title=The Biochemical Basis of an All-or-None Cell Fate Switch in Xenopus Oocytes |journal=Science |volume=280 |issue=5365 |pages=895–8 |year=1998 |last1=Ferrell Jr |first1=J. E |last2=Machleder |first2=E. M |bibcode=1998Sci...280..895F }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/science.280.5365.852 |pmid=9599157 |title=BIOCHEMISTRY: Enhanced: The Era of Pathway Quantification |journal=Science |volume=280 |issue=5365 |pages=852–3 |year=1998 |last1=Koshland Jr |first1=D. E |s2cid=26301778 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1038/nature02089 |pmid=14647386 |title=A positive-feedback-based bistable 'memory module' that governs a cell fate decision |journal=Nature |volume=426 |issue=6965 |pages=460–5 |year=2003 |last1=Xiong |first1=Wen |last2=Ferrell |first2=James E |bibcode=2003Natur.426..460X |s2cid=4396489 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1038/426392a |pmid=14647363 |title=Cell biology: Thanks for the memory |journal=Nature |volume=426 |issue=6965 |pages=392–3 |year=2003 |last1=Sible |first1=Jill C |bibcode=2003Natur.426..392S |doi-access=free }}</ref>  These studies helped demonstrate how ultrasensitivity, positive feedback, and bistability can allow cells to switch between discrete states.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=2002-04-01|title=Self-perpetuating states in signal transduction: positive feedback, double-negative feedback and bistability|journal=Current Opinion in Cell Biology|language=en|volume=14|issue=2|pages=140–148|doi=10.1016/S0955-0674(02)00314-9|issn=0955-0674|last1=Ferrell|first1=James E.|pmid=11891111}}</ref>

Subsequent work from the Ferrell lab<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1038/ncb954 |pmid=12629549 |title=Building a cell cycle oscillator: Hysteresis and bistability in the activation of Cdc2 |journal=Nature Cell Biology |volume=5 |issue=4 |pages=346–51 |year=2003 |last1=Pomerening |first1=Joseph R |last2=Sontag |first2=Eduardo D |last3=Ferrell |first3=James E |s2cid=11047458 }}</ref> and others<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1073/pnas.0235349100 |pmid=12509509 |pmc=298711 |title=Hysteresis drives cell-cycle transitions in Xenopus laevis egg extracts |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=100 |issue=3 |pages=975–80 |year=2002 |last1=Sha |first1=W |last2=Moore |first2=J |last3=Chen |first3=K |last4=Lassaletta |first4=A. D |last5=Yi |first5=C.-S |last6=Tyson |first6=J. J |last7=Sible |first7=J. C |doi-access=free }}</ref> demonstrated that the cell cycle transition between interphase and mitosis is regulated by a bistable switch, and that the Xenopus early embryonic cell cycle operates like a relaxation oscillator.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.cell.2005.06.016 |pmid=16122424 |title=Systems-Level Dissection of the Cell-Cycle Oscillator: Bypassing Positive Feedback Produces Damped Oscillations |journal=Cell |volume=122 |issue=4 |pages=565–78 |year=2005 |last1=Pomerening |first1=Joseph R |last2=Kim |first2=Sun Young |last3=Ferrell |first3=James E |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1016/j.devcel.2005.08.006 |pmid=16139219 |title=Shake It, Don't Break It: Positive Feedback and the Evolution of Oscillator Design |journal=Developmental Cell |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=309–10 |year=2005 |last1=Cross |first1=Frederick R |last2=Siggia |first2=Eric D |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/stke.3162006eg1 |pmid=16391177 |title=2005: Signaling Breakthroughs of the Year |journal=Science Signaling |volume=2006 |issue=316 |article-number=eg1 |year=2005 |last1=Adler |first1=E. M |last2=Gough |first2=N. R |last3=Ray |first3=L. B |s2cid=45634327 }}</ref> These findings helped validate earlier theoretical predictions and modeling studies.<ref>{{cite journal |pmid=8126097 |url=http://jcs.biologists.org/cgi/pmidlookup?view=long&pmid=8126097 |year=1993 |last1=Novak |first1=B |title=Numerical analysis of a comprehensive model of M-phase control in Xenopus oocyte extracts and intact embryos |journal=Journal of Cell Science |volume=106 |issue=4 |pages=1153–68 |last2=Tyson |first2=J. J |doi = 10.1242/jcs.106.4.1153|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Goldbeter |first1=A |title=Modeling the mitotic oscillator driving the cell division cycle |year=1993 |journal=Comments on Theoretical Biology |volume=3 |pages=75–107 }}</ref>

Recently the Ferrell lab showed that the mitotic state can propagate through Xenopus cytoplasm via trigger waves, waves of Cdk1 activity that spread faster and farther than the Cdk1 protein molecules can diffuse.<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1038/nature12321 |pmid=23863935 |pmc=3758429 |title=Mitotic trigger waves and the spatial coordination of the Xenopus cell cycle |journal=Nature |volume=500 |issue=7464 |pages=603–7 |year=2013 |last1=Chang |first1=Jeremy B |last2=Ferrell Jr |first2=James E |bibcode=2013Natur.500..603C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1098/rstb.2013.0454 |pmid=25047608 |pmc=4113098 |title=Organization of early frog embryos by chemical waves emanating from centrosomes |journal=Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences |volume=369 |issue=1650 |article-number=20130454 |year=2014 |last1=Ishihara |first1=K |last2=Nguyen |first2=P. A |last3=Wuhr |first3=M |last4=Groen |first4=A. C |last5=Field |first5=C. M |last6=Mitchison |first6=T. J }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1126/scisignal.2005013 |pmid=24399293 |title=2013: Signaling Breakthroughs of the Year |journal=Science Signaling |volume=7 |issue=307 |pages=eg1 |year=2014 |last1=Berndt |first1=J. D |last2=Gough |first2=N. R |s2cid=40864652 }}</ref> They also showed that apoptosis propagates through cytoplasm by trigger waves; the "speed of death" is about 2 mm per hour.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cheng|first1=Xianrui|last2=Ferrell|first2=James E.|date=2018-08-10|title=Apoptosis propagates through the cytoplasm as trigger waves|url= |journal=Science|language=en|volume=361|issue=6402|pages=607–612|doi=10.1126/science.aah4065|issn=0036-8075|pmid=30093599|pmc=6263143|bibcode=2018Sci...361..607C}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cosmosmagazine.com/biology/for-unwanted-cells-death-comes-in-waves|title=For unwanted cells, death comes in waves {{!}} Cosmos|website=cosmosmagazine.com|date=9 August 2018|language=en|access-date=2018-09-18}}</ref>
